newsitem.title: USA: Ocean Reef withdraws Best Products buyout offer.
newsitem.headline: Ocean Reef withdraws Best Products buyout offer.

text.p: Best Products Co. Inc. said Monday that Ocean Reef Management Inc. has formally withdrawn its friendly offer to acquire the troubled catalogue retailer for about $63.2 million.
Ocean Reef, an investment firm, offered to buy Best Products for $2 a share on Sept. 3, saying the Richmond, Va.-based chain of 169 showroom stores presented an opportunity for a turnaround.
But Ocean Reef concluded that Best requires greater resources than it originally expected, the retailer said.
Ocean Reef indicated it wanted to continue discussions and said it may develop an alternative proposal, Best added.

Best, which emerged from Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in June 1994, said it is delaying payments and the receipt of certain merchandise shipments from vendors as it explores all options available to it.
Industry analysts and vendors have said Best is at a critical juncture and either needs to be sold or seek bankruptcy protection again.

Best, which pioneered the catalogue retail store format in 1957, got into trouble in the 1980s as competition grew. It became saddled with debt after a leveraged buyout in 1988. It has lost money in the past four quarters and reported a $95.6 million loss for 1995, including restructuring charges of $45.7 million.
Ocean Reef recently acquired a controlling interest in L. Luria & Son Inc., another catalogue retailer that sells jewelry and home furnishings.
Best's stock fell 37.5 cents to 68.75 cents early on Nasdaq.
